text_blocks.snippet: There are two main types of flu vaccines: inactivated influenza vaccines (IIV) and live attenuated influenza vaccines (LAIV). IIV are injectable and contain killed flu viruses, while LAIV is administered as a nasal spray and contains live, weakened (attenuated) flu viruses. Both types can be further categorized into trivalent (protecting against three virus strains) or quadrivalent (protecting against four).
snippet_highlighted_words: inactivated influenza vaccines (IIV) and live attenuated influenza vaccines (LAIV)

list.title: Injectable:
list.snippet: These are the most common type of flu vaccine and are administered via injection, typically into the muscle (intramuscular).

list.title: Trivalent or Quadrivalent:
list.snippet: IIVs can be either trivalent, protecting against three strains of influenza (A(H1N1), A(H3N2), and one B lineage), or quadrivalent, adding a second B lineage virus.

list.title: Egg-based and Cell-based:
list.snippet: IIVs can be produced using either chicken eggs or cell cultures.
